# Actual source faces, common projective charts, and exact row budgets

This continues the source-preserving canonical plane reduction. It uses
the ACTUAL proper deepest interpolation equalities, full marked-energy
equality classification, and unchanged parameter rows. It proves a common
projective field on each source face without assuming a globally positive
affine scale in advance. It also gives the exact original-volume mass,
first-moment, and entropy identities after the new chart tilt.

No identity below bounds the outside-contact surface erosion by that
volume budget. The last section identifies the precise missing comparison.

## 1. Standing source face and marked homothety

Use the actual standing hypotheses of
canonical-source-parity-plane-reduction-and-certificate-contraction-optimal-midpoint.md.
Let Q be one maximal occupied face of the positive source-base hull,
q in relint Q an integer anchor, and I_Q the positive original source
bases on Q. Every point of I_Q is a proper deepest base with its unique
mark Y_i=(p_i,y_i). Write

    F(z,x)=E_(C_z)(x)^(1/d),   F_i=F(Y_i),   L_i=L(Y_i)>0.

The active proper quantile at an integer interpolation gives equality
in the concavity of

    [L F^d]^(1/(d+1)).

Since both L and F are positive and concave, equality in the positive
weighted geometric mean forces equality separately in L and F and
forces the positive pairs (L_i,F_i) to be proportional. The equality
classification of the jointly concave energy, including its strict
inclusion step, therefore gives, for every positive-weight integer
anchored representation using these sources,

    Y_p=sum_i theta_i Y_i,
    K_p=sum_i theta_i K_p_i,
    (K_p_i-y_i)/F_i is independent of i,
    F_i/L_i is independent of i.                         (1)

The joint-energy equality and strict-inclusion inputs are proved in
candidate 5811f0ad1132ce56
and projective-energy-maximal-deepest-stratum-and-marked-fiber-rigidity-slab-recovery.md.
No equality for an arbitrary source-to-target row is inferred.

Choose a reference i_* in I_Q and put

    D=K_p_i_* - y_i_*,
    E_*=E_D(0),     L_*=L_i_*,
    ell_i=F_i/E_*^(1/d)=L_i/L_*.

Then D contains 0 in its interior, and applying (1) at q using ALL
source bases in Q with positive weights gives

    K_p_i=y_i+ell_i D for every i in I_Q.                 (2)

## 2. The marked graph and the scale are affine on the entire face

There are affine maps y:aff Q -> R^d and ell:aff Q -> R such that
y(p_i)=y_i and ell(p_i)=ell_i. In particular ell>0 on Q.

To prove the affine consistency, represent q by strictly positive
coefficients theta_i on all of I_Q. If numbers beta_i satisfy

    sum beta_i=0,    sum beta_i p_i=0,

then theta_i+t beta_i stay positive for both signs of sufficiently
small t. Every such representation has the SAME integer target q.
The unique proper deepest mark there and (1) imply

    sum beta_i y_i=0,    sum beta_i F_i=0.

Thus both the y_i values and the ell_i values respect every affine
dependence among their bases. This proves the asserted affine maps.

In fact the ACTUAL real fibers satisfy

    C_z=y(z)+ell(z)D for EVERY real z in Q.                (3)

First, every z in Q is a convex combination of the source bases, so
actual convexity and (2) give inclusion of the displayed body in C_z.
To prove the reverse inclusion fix a continuous unit normal u.
The actual support profile h(z)=h_(C_z)(u) is concave in z. Its
finite-hull support LP has a finite affine majorant B_u touching at q.
By the exact equality K_q=y(q)+ell(q)D,

    B_u(q)=u dot y(q)+ell(q)h_D(u).

Its gaps above the supports at the source bases are nonnegative and
have positive weighted average zero. Thus B_u agrees at ALL source
bases with the affine function u dot y(z)+ell(z)h_D(u), hence agrees
on Q. Therefore h(z) is at most that same function on Q. The first
inclusion gives the opposite inequality. Equality for every u proves
(3).

This argument does not assume Q is a face of the FULL original base
projection. Extra original fibers outside Q can contribute to real
sections over Q, but the supporting equality at its integer interior
anchor prevents them from making these sections larger.

## 3. A positive BASE-affine scale extension always exists

Let B=conv(P) be the full original base projection and define

    v(z)=|C_z|^(1/d)/|D|^(1/d),      z in B.

This is a positive concave function by ordinary Brunn--Minkowski.
By (3), v=ell on Q. There is a finite affine majorant

    a_Q(z)>=v(z) on B,     a_Q(q)=v(q).                  (4)

It follows that a_Q=ell throughout Q, and a_Q has a strictly positive
minimum over B.

Here are the boundary-base details of existence and positivity.
Canonical finite-hull fibers are uniformly Hausdorff-Lipschitz in z,
by the fixed finite support LP proved in
candidate c0fc791108fc8765,
Section 3. They also have a uniform positive inradius: combine balls
of one common radius in the finitely many sampled fibers.
For close fibers, their symmetric-difference volumes are bounded by
a constant times their Hausdorff distance. This follows from inclusion
in dilations by 1+delta/r about a common interior ball, locally, and a
finite cover of the compact base. Their volumes are uniformly bounded
away from zero. Thus v is locally Lipschitz relative to B, including
its boundary.

A finite supergradient at q follows by the elementary convex extension
argument. On a small closed convex neighborhood in B, the convex
function -v is Lipschitz. Its infimal-convolution extension by a large
multiple of the Euclidean norm is finite convex on the full relative
base space and agrees with -v on that neighborhood. A subgradient at
q yields a local affine upper support of v. Concavity along segments
extends that support to all B, proving (4).

The affine nonnegative gap a_Q-ell on Q vanishes at q in relint Q,
so it vanishes throughout Q. The uniform inradius gives v>=c>0;
(4) therefore makes a_Q>=c>0 on the entire B.

This is a BASE-affine function. It is generally different from the
canonical parameter plane touching these sources.

## 4. One genuine projective denominator and support mask

Let a_* be the unique ordinary projective normalizer of (D,0).
The global energy-supergradient theorem supplies an affine S_Q
majorizing F on C and touching it at Y_q. Its continuous coefficient
is ((d+1)/d)E_*^(1/d)a_*. Equality on the marked graph of (3) implies

    S_Q(z,x)/E_*^(1/d)
      =ell(z)+((d+1)/d)a_* dot(x-y(z)),   z in Q.          (5)

Define the common affine denominator

    R_Q(z,x)= [d/(d+1)] S_Q(z,x)/E_*^(1/d)
                         +a_Q(z)/(d+1).                (6)

The energy majorant is nonnegative on C by interior-fiber
approximation, and a_Q has a positive minimum. Hence
R_Q>=min_B a_Q/(d+1)>0 on all C. On Q,

    R_Q(z,x)=ell(z)+a_* dot(x-y(z)).                      (7)

Consequently R_Q/ell_i is the EXACT projective normalizer of the
marked source fiber (K_p_i,y_i), not merely a positive denominator.

For each normal u choose the same affine support majorant B_u of
Section 2. It touches every actual fiber over Q. The scaled source
erosion potentials agree throughout C:

    ell_i^(-(d+1)) [ell_i h_D(u)]
                         [R_Q/ell_i]^(-d)
       =h_D(u)/R_Q^d.                                  (8)

One common tangent continuation below the global positivity floor
keeps (8) valid in the globally convex cut construction. Thus all
sources on Q can use identical physical supporting cuts. Their
common first normal speed is

    v_Q(z,x)=1_(B_n(z)=h_(C_z)(n)) h_D(n)/R_Q(z,x)^d    (9)

at regular boundary points with outward normal n. The common contact
mask is preserved by midpoint averaging because B_u is affine and
globally majorizes the actual support.

This is exactly the common-weight situation required by the proved
normal-conditional weighted surface repair. It does not involve a
maximum of different denominators within Q.

### Warning about two different affine functions

Let B_Q(z,x) be the canonical PARAMETER plane touching the source
marks on Q. Usually it has a nonzero continuous coefficient c_Q.
One must not substitute B_Q/L_* for the BASE-affine function a_Q in
(6). On a source fiber that substitution yields

    ell_i+[a_*+c_Q/((d+1)L_*)] dot(x-y_i),

rather than (7). Its projective image need not have centroid at the
marked source, so the ordinary Gamma_d cap credit is not supplied.
The positive base-affine extension in Section 3 avoids this error.

## 5. Retain original whole rows and assign each to one touching face

The maximal occupied faces can overlap. Assign each ORIGINAL positive
source to one face containing its base, for example the first such
face in a fixed order. Assign its ENTIRE old row to that face; no
pointwise target reallocation is performed.

Let nu_i be the unnormalized old row, so

    nu_i(C)=m_i=sigma_i/L_i,
    integral w dnu_i=m_i Y_i,
    integral L dnu_i=m_i L_i=sigma_i.

For a face Q sum only its assigned rows and write

    nu_Q=sum_(i assigned Q) nu_i,
    eta_Q=L nu_Q,           s_Q=sum_(i assigned Q) sigma_i.

Then

    sum_Q nu_Q=nu=dm/(M L),
    sum_Q eta_Q=dm/M,      eta_Q(C)=s_Q,  sum_Q s_Q=1.   (10)

The measures eta_Q are an exact partition by fractional densities of
ORIGINAL mixed volume. Distinct eta_Q may have overlapping supports.
Their sum identity, rather than support disjointness, is the budget.

Because B_Q touches every source in Q, the actual row contact equality
gives

    L=B_Q   nu_Q-almost everywhere.                    (11)

Here one uses the new canonical PL extension if needed, so B_Q is
a global majorant. Equivalently the same equality on the sampled row
support is sufficient for every integral below.

## 6. The new chart tilt has exact mass and an explicit drift

Set W_Q=L_* R_Q. This is a positive affine function and
W_Q(Y_i)=L_i for every assigned source. Define

    hat_eta_Q=W_Q nu_Q
              =(W_Q/L) eta_Q.                          (12)

The actual affine barycenter equations give the exact mass identity

    hat_eta_Q(C)=sum_i m_i W_Q(Y_i)=s_Q=eta_Q(C).         (13)

Thus no parity loss occurs in this volume normalization. The total
mass of all new tilted pieces is one.

However this does NOT say their sum is dm/M, or that each retains its
original first moment. Their full first-moment difference is explicit.
Put rho_i=nu_i/m_i and

    Cov_i=integral (w-Y_i)(w-Y_i)^T d rho_i,
    b_Q=gradient(W_Q-B_Q).

Since the affine function W_Q-B_Q vanishes at every assigned source,
(11) and the old row mean give

    integral w d(hat_eta_Q-eta_Q)
       =sum_(i assigned Q) m_i Cov_i b_Q.               (14)

This includes the integer coordinates. In general the vector in
(14) is not zero. It cannot be suppressed by calling the new tilt
another martingale or an original-volume-preserving transport.

There is also a genuine exact entropy defect. For s_Q>0 put
g_Q=W_Q/L. Equation (13) says integral g_Q d eta_Q=s_Q.
Logarithmic Jensen yields

    integral log g_Q d eta_Q <=0,
    D(eta_Q || hat_eta_Q)
       =-integral log g_Q d eta_Q >=0.                 (15)

Both measures have the same finite mass. Strict positivity and
compactness make these quantities finite in the present fixed-body
setting. Equality holds exactly when g_Q=1 eta_Q-almost everywhere.
Likewise D(hat_eta_Q || eta_Q)=integral g_Q log g_Q d eta_Q>=0.

The source-weighted total prescribed OWN-fiber cost of the common
field is another exact identity:

    sum_(i assigned Q) sigma_i D_i^common
       =d E_* sum_i sigma_i/ell_i
       =d E_* L_* nu_Q(C),                             (16)

because D_i^common=d E_*/ell_i. This is proportional to the TILTED
row mass nu_Q(C), not to original-volume allocation s_Q. Ordinary
projective-centroid Grünbaum pays Gamma_d times each D_i^common
for every cap containing that source; (16) does not change the
physical response weights of the original separator.

## 7. What an outside-contact payment still has to prove

The physical total cost for (9) is

    D_Q^surface=sum_z integral_(boundary K_z) v_Q dS.   (17)

Equations (10)--(16) concern actual VOLUME rows and affine chart
tilts. They do not identify (17) with s_Q, nu_Q(C), or the own costs
in (16). The common supporting cuts can act on contact fibers outside
Q. Their normal and tangential surface densities are not the volume
row densities eta_Q. The weighted surface repair theorem applies to
an actual supplied normal-preserving endpoint coupling; (10) alone
does not supply one with those marginals.

The useful new structure is now precise: at most k(P) source faces
have actual common projective fields; the old full rows are retained;
their new chart tilts have exactly the same allocated original mass,
with the explicit covariance drift (14) and entropy defect (15).
A successful aggregate payment would have to connect the outside
surface cost or its selected cap credit to these exact row quantities
using the SAME physical separator. No such comparison is asserted
here, and no generic maximum-field counterexample is used to reject
it under the stronger canonical hypotheses.
